# SECTION: TYPESCRIPT SDK AGENT (typescript-sdk/agent.mdx)

---
title: "LIOP Agent (CLI)"
description: "Zero-Config security gateway for desktop AI applications"
icon: "bot"

---

The **LIOP Agent** is a pre-compiled, production-ready CLI utility included with the `@nekzus/liop` package. It acts as a bridge between standard AI interfaces (like **Claude Desktop** or **Cursor**) and the decentralized **Logic-Injection-on-Origin Protocol**.

Instead of writing a custom server, users can simply run the agent to instantly gain "Logic-Injection-on-Origin" capabilities.

## Installation

The agent is distributed via the main SDK package. You can run it directly using `npx`:

```bash
npx -y @nekzus/liop@latest
```

Or install it globally to have the `liop` command available system-wide:

```bash
npm install -g @nekzus/liop@latest
liop
```

## 🤖 Claude Desktop Integration

LIOP is designed to be a drop-in replacement for MCP servers. To add LIOP tools to your Claude Desktop experience, update your configuration file:

<CodeGroup>
```json Windows (%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json)
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "liop": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@nekzus/liop@latest"],
      "env": {
        "LIOP_NEXUS_URL": "http://your-nexus-host:3000",
        "LIOP_TOKEN_BANK": "your-bank-token-here",
        "LIOP_TOKEN_VAULT": "your-vault-token-here",
        "LIOP_LOG_LEVEL": "info",
        "NODE_OPTIONS": "--use-system-ca"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
```json macOS (~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json)
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "liop": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@nekzus/liop@latest"],
      "env": {
        "LIOP_NEXUS_URL": "http://your-nexus-host:3000",
        "LIOP_TOKEN_BANK": "your-bank-token-here",
        "LIOP_TOKEN_VAULT": "your-vault-token-here",
        "LIOP_LOG_LEVEL": "info",
        "NODE_OPTIONS": "--use-system-ca"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

Once configured, restart Claude Desktop. You will see the 🛡️ **LIOP Guard** status in your logs.

## Core Features

### 1. Identity Persistence
The agent generates a unique **PeerID** (Ed25519 keypair) the first time it runs. This identity is stored in:
`~/.liop/identity.json`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If you move to a different machine, copying this folder will allow you to keep your reputation and verified access across the Mesh.

### 2. Autonomous Routing
The agent uses the `LiopMcpRouter` internally. When a tool call is received from Claude:
1. It queries the **Kademlia DHT** to find nodes providing that tool.
2. It establishes a **Kyber768 + AES-256-GCM** secure tunnel.
3. It executes the logic on the remote server and returns the verified result.

### 3. Bootstrap Discovery
By default, the agent connects to the official **LIOP Alpha Nexus**. However, you can point it to any mesh bootstrap node:

```bash
npx @nekzus/liop@latest /ip4/1.2.3.4/tcp/4001/p2p/PEER_ID
```

## Security & Diagnostics
The agent only communicates via **STDIO**. It prints status logs and discovery events strictly to `stderr`, ensuring that the `stdout` channel remains clean for valid JSON-RPC 2.0 messages required by the LLM client.

### Local Mesh Diagnostics (`LiopMeshStatus`)
The agent automatically exposes a local diagnostic tool called **`LiopMeshStatus`**. When an LLM calls this tool, the agent intercepts it locally instead of routing it over the P2P network. It returns a structured operational report detailing:
- Connected Bootstrappers and Peer IDs
- Active Nodes (Vault, Bank, Oracle)
- Tool routing tables and Kademlia DHT state
- Token consumption and telemetry estimates

This allows AI clients to autonomously diagnose connection drops or verify which tools are available without generating unnecessary network traffic or duplicating diagnostic requests across multiple nodes.

### Environment Variables

The agent behavior can be customized via the following environment variables:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|:---------|:--------|:------------|
| `LIOP_NEXUS_URL` | *(none)* | URL of the Nexus node for Auto-Discovery. The agent resolves the PeerID and multiaddr from the `/health` endpoint automatically |
| `LIOP_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | Controls log verbosity (`silent`, `info`, `debug`). Set to `silent` to suppress all stderr output |
| `LIOP_EXPECTED_PROVIDERS` | `1` | Number of mesh providers to wait for during initial warm-up. The adaptive DHT polling continues discovering additional providers in the background |
| `LIOP_INITIAL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `8000` | Maximum time (ms) to wait for the initial mesh discovery phase before proceeding |
| `LIOP_MCP_COMPACT_TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS` | `true` | Strips verbose protocol metadata from tool descriptions, reducing token consumption by ~500 tokens per tool. Set to `0` to opt-out |
| `LIOP_GRPC_PORT` | `50051` | Override the default gRPC port for the internal RPC server |
| `LIOP_WORKER_MAX_HEAP_MB` | `64` | Maximum V8 heap size per worker thread (Heap Bomb defense) |
| `LIOP_QUERY_BUDGET` | *(none)* | Session query budget override for high-frequency analytical audit testing |
| `LIOP_DOCKER_MAP` | `false` | Force translation of Docker-internal container IPs (`172.x.x.x`) to the host loopback (`127.0.0.1`), mapping target gRPC services to host-published ports for running containerized mesh nodes in local environments |
| `LIOP_DEV_MODE` | `false` | Enables development heuristics, which automatically activates Docker port mapping if the Nexus URL points to local demo ports (`13000`/`13001`) |
| `LIOP_DATASET_SCALE` | `1` | Scaling factor used by test and demo nodes to dynamically scale synthetic record generation size (e.g., bank transactions, health records) |

### Dual-Era MCP Handshake Compliance

The LIOP Agent natively satisfies both modern and legacy MCP client protocols:

- **MCP v2 Revision (2026-07-28)**:
  - Answers `server/discover` probes without authentication for stateless tool discovery.
  - Automatically includes mandatory `resultType: "complete"` in `tools/list` responses.
  - Handles `subscriptions/listen` and `resources/templates/list` without polling overhead.
- **MCP Legacy Era (2025-11-25)**:
  - Strips v2 metadata via `adaptResponseForLegacyClient()` to prevent parsing failures in legacy desktop clients.

<Warning>
  `LIOP_BOOTSTRAP_FILE` is **deprecated** since v2.0.0-alpha. Use `LIOP_NEXUS_URL` instead. The agent will log a warning if this variable is detected.
</Warning>

---

## Programmatic Mesh Integration (`MeshNode`)

Developers integrating LIOP into custom backend services can instantiate and manage `MeshNode` directly rather than invoking the CLI binary:

```typescript
import { MeshNode } from "@nekzus/liop";

const mesh = new MeshNode({
  listenAddresses: ["/ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/4001"],
  bootstrapNodes: [
    "/ip4/127.0.0.1/tcp/15001/p2p/12D3KooW..."
  ],
  enableWAN: false,
  enableAutoNAT: true,
  enableRelay: true,
});

await mesh.start();
console.log("Local Peer ID:", mesh.getPeerId());

// Discover remote enclaves announcing a specific tool capability
const providers = await mesh.findProviders("tool:execute_anomaly_audit");

// Query a remote node's capability manifest over /liop/manifest/1.0.0
for (const peerId of providers) {
  const manifest = await mesh.queryManifest(peerId);
  console.log(`Discovered ${manifest?.tools.length} tools on ${peerId}`);
}

// Graceful shutdown
await mesh.stop();
```

### Key Public Methods

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `start()` | `Promise<void>` | Initializes libp2p transports, Noise crypto, and Kademlia routing |
| `stop()` | `Promise<void>` | Closes all active swarm sockets and flushes DHT routing state |
| `getPeerId()` | `string` | Returns the local node's Ed25519 Peer ID string |
| `getMultiaddrs()` | `string[]` | Returns all bound transport multiaddrs (TCP/WS) |
| `findProviders(capability)` | `Promise<string[]>` | Queries Kademlia DHT for peer IDs advertising a capability |
| `queryManifest(target)` | `Promise<LiopManifest \| null>` | Directly fetches signed JSON manifest from a remote peer |
| `announceManifest(manifest)` | `Promise<void>` | Publishes local capabilities to the DHT and registers manifest stream handler |

If you encounter connection issues, check for the 🛡️ icon in the console or ask the LLM to call `LiopMeshStatus`.

# SECTION: TYPESCRIPT SDK CLIENT (typescript-sdk/client.mdx)

---
title: "LiopClient"
description: "High-level orchestration for intent routing, peer discovery, and in-situ logic execution"
icon: "terminal"

---

The `LiopClient` class acts as the primary dispatch coordinator for Agent Nodes in the Logic-Injection-on-Origin Protocol. It manages transport negotiation across heterogeneous topologies (direct HTTP/JSON-RPC gateways, authenticated perimeter proxies, and sovereign P2P gRPC channels), executes cryptographic handshakes, and dispatches WebAssembly or JavaScript logic modules to remote Data Nodes.

Unlike traditional Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients that pull massive raw datasets across the network via polling or streaming endpoints, `LiopClient` packages analytical intent into isolated micro-modules and transmits them directly to where the data resides.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client["LiopClient Orchestration Layer"]
        direction LR
        subgraph Auth["Auth Layer"]
            A1["TokenManager (OAuth 2.1 M2M)"]
            A2["RFC 8707 Resource Indicators"]
        end
        subgraph Discovery["Discovery Layer"]
            D1["Kademlia DHT / MDNS"]
            D2["RFC 9728 TopologyProbe"]
        end
        subgraph Transport["Transport Layer"]
            T1["Tonic gRPC (HTTP/2)"]
            T2["ML-KEM-768 (Kyber PQC)"]
        end
    end
    Client -->|Perimeter HTTP/2| Gateway["Perimeter HTTP Gateway\n(Border LIO Gateway :15018)"]
    Client -->|Direct gRPC Mesh| Enclave["Sovereign P2P Enclave\n(Direct Vault / Bank Node)"]
```

---

## Constructor & Configuration

The constructor configures the transport-level TLS credentials applied to all underlying gRPC connections.

```typescript
import { LiopClient } from "@nekzus/liop";
import type { LiopTlsOptions } from "@nekzus/liop";

const tls: LiopTlsOptions = {
  rootCertPath: "/etc/ssl/certs/liop-ca.pem",
  clientCertPath: "/etc/ssl/certs/agent-client.pem",
  clientKeyPath: "/etc/ssl/private/agent-key.pem",
  serverNameOverride: "mesh.enclave.internal",
};

const client = new LiopClient(tls);
```

### Constructor Parameters

<ParamField path="tls" type="LiopTlsOptions" optional>
  Cryptographic credentials for mutual TLS (mTLS) or server verification over gRPC transport.
  
  <Expandable title="LiopTlsOptions Properties">
    <ResponseField name="rootCertPath" type="string" optional>
      Filesystem path to the root CA certificate used to validate server identity.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="clientCertPath" type="string" optional>
      Filesystem path to the client certificate for mTLS client authentication.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="clientKeyPath" type="string" optional>
      Filesystem path to the private key corresponding to `clientCertPath`.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="serverNameOverride" type="string" optional>
      Overrides the expected SNI server name when connecting through internal proxies or container networks.
    </ResponseField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

---

## Connecting to the Mesh (`connect`)

The `connect()` method establishes identity, provisions machine-to-machine (M2M) OAuth 2.1 tokens, and mounts either a direct point-to-point gRPC channel or a distributed libp2p node.

```typescript
// Pattern A: Connecting to a specific gateway or enclave address
await client.connect("127.0.0.1:15021", {
  auth: {
    clientId: "analytics-agent-01",
    clientSecret: process.env.LIOP_CLIENT_SECRET,
    nexusUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:15000",
    audience: "urn:liop:mesh:api",
    scope: "liop:tools:call liop:tools:list",
  },
});

// Pattern B: Connecting dynamically to the P2P Mesh backbone
await client.connect(undefined, {
  meshConfig: {
    bootstrapNodes: [
      "/ip4/198.51.100.10/tcp/15001/p2p/12D3KooWDpJ7As7BWAwRMfu1VU2WCqNjvq387JEYKDBj4kx6nXTN"
    ],
    listenAddresses: ["/ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/0"],
  },
});
```

### Connection Options

<ParamField path="address" type="string" optional>
  Target endpoint in `host:port` format. When specified, creates a direct high-speed `LiopRpcClient` targeting that endpoint. When omitted, `LiopClient` routes requests dynamically through the peer-to-peer DHT.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="options" type="object" optional>
  Advanced connection settings covering authentication and peer-to-peer discovery.

  <Expandable title="Connection Options Properties">
    <ResponseField name="auth.clientId" type="string" optional>
      OAuth 2.1 client identifier registered with the Nexus OIDC authorization server. Falls back to `process.env.LIOP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="auth.clientSecret" type="string" optional>
      Client secret for the RFC 6749 Client Credentials grant. Falls back to `process.env.LIOP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="auth.nexusUrl" type="string" optional>
      Base URL of the OIDC Identity Provider (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:15000`). Automatically normalizes `/oidc/token` endpoints.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="auth.audience" type="string" optional>
      RFC 8707 Resource Indicator targeting the destination enclave (default: `urn:liop:mesh:api`).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="auth.scope" type="string" optional>
      Space-delimited OAuth 2.1 scopes required for execution. Defaults to standard capability scopes.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="auth.token" type="string" optional>
      Pre-computed static Bearer token. Bypasses the dynamic `TokenManager` handshake when supplied.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="meshConfig" type="MeshNodeConfig" optional>
      Configuration object for the underlying `libp2p` instance, including bootstrap multiaddrs and swarm keys.
    </ResponseField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

---

## Capability Discovery & Tool Invocations

`LiopClient` unifies tool discovery and execution under standard MCP schema shapes while enforcing post-quantum transport security under the hood.

```typescript
// 1. Discover all tools registered across connected peers
const tools = await client.discoverTools();
console.log(`Discovered ${tools.length} mesh tools`);

// 2. Resolve capability target peer
const targetPeer = await client.resolveCapability("Analyze_Bank_Ledger");

// 3. Invoke tool with in-situ logic
const response = await client.callTool({
  name: "Analyze_Bank_Ledger",
  arguments: {
    account_id: "ACC-88219",
    currency: "USD",
    min_amount: 10000,
  },
});

for (const item of response.content) {
  if (item.type === "text") {
    console.log("Analytical Result:", item.text);
  }
}
```

### In-Situ Logic Injection (WASM Bytecode)

For zero-data-movement pipelines, pass compiled WebAssembly bytecode directly via the optional second argument of `callTool()`. The remote enclave validates the bytecode through Guardian AST before executing it in an isolated V8 sandbox.

```typescript
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const wasmBinary = readFileSync("./aggregators/p99_latency.wasm");

const result = await client.callTool(
  {
    name: "Query_Telemetry_Logs",
    arguments: { service: "auth-gateway", window: "1h" },
  },
  wasmBinary, // Injected logic executed at the origin
);
```

---

## Mathematical Verification (ZK-Receipts)

Every analytical payload executed by a compliant LIOP Data Node generates a cryptographic ZK-Receipt (HMAC-SHA256 sealed under the ephemeral ML-KEM-768 session secret). `LiopClient` validates this proof automatically during `callTool()`.

To manually verify proofs received out-of-band:

```typescript
const isValid = await client.verifier.verifyZkReceipt(
  wasmPayload,          // Buffer containing the exact injected code
  remoteImageIdHex,     // Expected hash of the data environment
  zkReceiptBuffer,      // Cryptographic receipt returned by the server
);

if (!isValid) {
  throw new Error("Zero-Trust Verification Failure: Computation tampering detected");
}
```

---

## Low-Level gRPC Transport (`LiopRpcClient`)

For applications that need fine-grained control over gRPC channels, metadata streaming, or token injection without spawning a P2P node, use `LiopRpcClient` directly:

```typescript
import { LiopRpcClient } from "@nekzus/liop";

const rpc = new LiopRpcClient(
  "127.0.0.1:15021",
  tlsConfig,
  async () => tokenManager.getToken(), // Dynamic async token resolver
);

// Step 1: Negotiate intent and acquire ephemeral Kyber public key
const intent = await rpc.negotiateIntent({
  capabilityName: "Analyze_Bank_Ledger",
  requesterPeerId: "12D3KooW...",
  clearanceLevel: 3,
});

// Step 2: Stream logic execution
const stream = rpc.executeLogic(encryptedLogicRequest);

stream.on("data", (response) => {
  console.log("Stream Chunk:", response.payload);
});
stream.on("error", (err) => {
  console.error("RPC Stream Error:", err);
});
```

### gRPC Channel Invariants

`LiopRpcClient` configures symmetric channel options to ensure long-running analytical queries do not drop across stateful NATs or corporate firewalls:

| Channel Option | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `grpc.keepalive_time_ms` | `30000` (30s) | Sends keepalive pings every 30 seconds to maintain open TCP state. |
| `grpc.keepalive_timeout_ms` | `10000` (10s) | Awaits ping acknowledgments for up to 10 seconds before declaring dropped connection. |
| `grpc.keepalive_permit_without_calls` | `1` | Allows keepalive pings even when no active RPC calls are inflight. |
| `grpc.http2.max_pings_without_data` | `0` | Eliminates ping burst limits to prevent aggressive proxy resets. |

---

## Public Methods Reference

| Method | Parameters | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connect(address?, options?)` | `address?: string`, `options?: ConnectOptions` | `Promise<void>` | Initializes discovery, acquires M2M tokens, and mounts transport channels. |
| `callTool(request, wasmBuffer?)` | `request: CallToolRequest`, `wasmBuffer?: Buffer` | `Promise<CallToolResult>` | Dispatches tool invocation with optional in-situ logic bytecode. |
| `discoverTools()` | None | `Promise<ToolDefinition[]>` | Queries connected peers and returns all advertised tool definitions. |
| `listTools()` | None | `Promise<ToolDefinition[]>` | Alias of `discoverTools()` providing 100% MCP client compatibility. |
| `resolveCapability(name)` | `name: string` | `Promise<string \| undefined>` | Resolves peer multiaddr or endpoint advertising the given tool name. |
| `getRoutingTable()` | None | `RoutingTable \| undefined` | Returns the active internal hybrid routing table instance. |
| `getMeshNode()` | None | `MeshNode \| null` | Returns the underlying `libp2p` node instance when connected in mesh mode. |
| `getServerInfo()` | None | `{ name: string; version: string } \| undefined` | Returns peer identification headers negotiated during handshake. |
| `close()` | None | `Promise<void>` | Gracefully terminates all active gRPC channels, worker pools, and P2P sockets. |

---

## Error Handling & Exception Catalog

`LiopClient` throws structured exceptions when security policies, authentication checks, or sandbox boundaries reject an execution.

```typescript
import { LiopError, ErrorCode } from "@nekzus/liop";

try {
  await client.callTool({
    name: "Analyze_Bank_Ledger",
    arguments: { query: "DROP TABLE users;" },
  });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof LiopError) {
    switch (error.code) {
      case ErrorCode.AST_SECURITY_VIOLATION:
        console.error("Layer 1 Rejection: Injected code accessed forbidden globals");
        break;
      case ErrorCode.UNAUTHENTICATED:
        console.error("Token Expired or Invalid: Check OAuth 2.1 credentials");
        break;
      case ErrorCode.CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN:
        console.warn("Peer is currently degraded. Rerouting to standby enclave");
        break;
      default:
        console.error(`Protocol Error [${error.code}]:`, error.message);
    }
  }
}
```

### Protocol Error Codes

| Error Code | HTTP / RPC Equivalence | Cause | Recommended Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | HTTP 401 / gRPC 16 | Missing, expired, or invalid OAuth 2.1 Bearer token. | Refresh credentials via `TokenManager.invalidate()`. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | HTTP 403 / gRPC 7 | Caller clearance tier does not meet resource taxonomy requirements. | Request scope elevation in Nexus OIDC console. |
| `AST_SECURITY_VIOLATION` | RPC -32099 / gRPC 3 | Guardian AST detected forbidden imports or poisoned globals. | Ensure bytecode complies with strict WASI Preview 1 allowlist. |
| `SANDBOX_HALTED` | RPC -32098 / gRPC 9 | V8 Isolate exceeded allocated CPU fuel or heap memory limits. | Optimize inner loops or raise `maxHeapMb` configuration. |
| `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN` | HTTP 503 / gRPC 14 | Target endpoint reached 5 consecutive failures (`MAX_FAILURES = 5`). | Wait for decay interval or use alternative gateway route. |
| `ZK_VERIFICATION_FAILED` | RPC -32097 / gRPC 10 | Output mathematical proof failed HMAC-SHA256 integrity seal. | Potential active network tampering. Drop response immediately. |


---

# SECTION: TYPESCRIPT SDK SERVER (typescript-sdk/server.mdx)

---
title: "LiopServer"
description: "High-security Data Node orchestration, sandboxed logic execution, and zero-trust capability hosting"
icon: "hard-drive"

---

The `LiopServer` class represents the host-side infrastructure of the Logic-Injection-on-Origin Protocol. It hosts sensitive datasets, enforces cryptographic boundaries, validates incoming WebAssembly or JavaScript logic modules via Guardian AST, and executes them inside isolated V8 sandboxes under strict CPU fuel and memory constraints.

Rather than exposing high-risk REST or SQL query endpoints to remote AI agents, a `LiopServer` exposes typed **Capabilities** (Tools). Agents submit compiled computation payloads to execute in-situ, ensuring raw rows never traverse the network.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Server["LiopServer Architecture"]
        direction LR
        subgraph Ingress["Ingress & Transport Layer"]
            I1["Tonic gRPC (HTTP/2) / mTLS"]
            I2["OAuth 2.1 RFC 8707 Validator"]
            I3["ML-KEM-768 Post-Quantum Key"]
            I4["Piscina Worker Pool (Crypto)"]
        end
        subgraph Shield["The Shield: Security Pipeline"]
            S1["Layer 1: Guardian AST (Allowlist)"]
            S2["Layer 2: V8 Sandbox (Poisoned Globals)"]
            S3["Layer 3: Taint Analyzer (IFC)"]
            S4["Layer 4: Egress PII Shield (Regex/NER)"]
            S5["Layer 5: Aggregation-First Policy"]
            S6["Layer 6: ZK-Receipt (HMAC-SHA256)"]
        end
    end
```

---

## Server Instantiation & Configuration

Initialize a Data Node by defining its identity and node characteristics:

```typescript
import { LiopServer, PII_PRESETS } from "@nekzus/liop";

const server = new LiopServer(
  {
    name: "ConfidentialBankEnclave",
    version: "2.4.0",
  },
  {
    tokenSlug: "BANK",
    port: 15021,
    workerPool: {
      enabled: true,
      maxThreads: 8,
      maxHeapMb: 128,
      idleTimeout: 30_000,
    },
    security: {
      forbiddenKeys: ["password", "secret", "privateKey", "cvv", "raw_balance"],
      piiPatterns: [
        ...PII_PRESETS.US_COMPLIANT,
        /[A-Z]{2}\d{6}[A-Z]/, // Internal clearance badge pattern
      ],
      enableNerScanning: true,
      rateLimit: {
        maxPerWindow: 60,
        windowMs: 60_000,
      },
    },
    taxonomy: {
      domain: "financial-ledger",
      clearanceTier: 4,
      executionTypes: ["aggregation", "statistical-audit"],
    },
  },
);
```

### Server Configuration Options

<ParamField path="serverInfo" type="object" required>
  Canonical identity announced during protocol handshakes.
  
  <Expandable title="serverInfo Properties">
    <ResponseField name="name" type="string" required>
      Identifier of the data node (e.g. `"EnterpriseVault"`).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="version" type="string" required>
      SemVer version string of the host deployment.
    </ResponseField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="options" type="ServerOptions" optional>
  Comprehensive security, thread scheduling, and taxonomy configurations.

  <Expandable title="ServerOptions Properties">
    <ResponseField name="port" type="number" optional>
      TCP port on which the gRPC transport binds (default: `50051`).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="tokenSlug" type="string" optional>
      Canonical uppercase identifier (e.g. `"BANK"`) used by clients to resolve authentication credentials dynamically (`LIOP_TOKEN_<tokenSlug>`). Must match `/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/`.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="workerPool.enabled" type="boolean" optional>
      When `true`, offloads cryptographic handshakes (ML-KEM-768) and AST parsing to a background `Piscina` worker pool (default: `true`).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="workerPool.maxThreads" type="number" optional>
      Maximum number of background worker threads spawned (default: available CPU cores).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="workerPool.maxHeapMb" type="number" optional>
      Hard heap limit per worker in megabytes to prevent memory exhaustion attacks (default: `64`). Configurable via `LIOP_WORKER_MAX_HEAP_MB`.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="security.forbiddenKeys" type="string[]" optional>
      JSON keys stripped or rejected if detected anywhere within the output object graph (default: `["password", "token", "secret", "privateKey"]`).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="security.piiPatterns" type="PiiRule[]" optional>
      Array of regex patterns or presets (`GLOBAL_STRICT`, `EU_GDPR`, `US_COMPLIANT`) scanned across all outgoing strings.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="security.enableNerScanning" type="boolean" optional>
      Enables Named Entity Recognition scanning on egress text using natural language processing to identify names, locations, and organizations (default: `false`).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="security.rateLimit" type="object" optional>
      Sliding window rate limiter per client peer (`maxPerWindow`, `windowMs`).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="taxonomy.domain" type="string" optional>
      Operational domain (e.g. `"healthcare"`, `"financial"`). Announced on the DHT for automatic routing.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="taxonomy.clearanceTier" type="number" optional>
      Required caller security clearance tier (`1` to `5`). Requests with insufficient clearance are rejected with HTTP 403.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="taxonomy.executionTypes" type="string[]" optional>
      Allowed compute types (`"aggregation"`, `"differential-privacy"`, `"analytics"`).
    </ResponseField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

---

## Defining Capabilities (`tool`)

Capabilities represent executable analytical tools exposed to the mesh. Define them with typed schemas using [Zod](https://zod.dev):

```typescript
import { z } from "zod";

server.tool(
  "Analyze_Account_Risk",
  "Computes statistical risk metrics for bank accounts without exporting raw ledger rows.",
  {
    accountId: z.string().regex(/^ACC-\d{5}$/, "Invalid account identifier"),
    timeframe: z.enum(["7d", "30d", "90d"]),
    thresholdAmount: z.number().positive(),
  },
  async ({ accountId, timeframe, thresholdAmount }) => {
    // 1. Fetch internal ledger from database
    const transactions = await db.fetchLedger(accountId, timeframe);

    // 2. Perform analytical calculation at the origin
    const highValueTxCount = transactions.filter(tx => tx.amount >= thresholdAmount).length;
    const avgVelocity = transactions.reduce((sum, tx) => sum + tx.amount, 0) / transactions.length;

    // 3. Return strictly aggregated results
    return {
      content: [
        {
          type: "text",
          text: JSON.stringify({
            accountId,
            highValueAlerts: highValueTxCount,
            meanTransactionVelocity: avgVelocity,
            riskScore: highValueTxCount > 5 ? "ELEVATED" : "NORMAL",
          }),
        },
      ],
    };
  },
);
```

### In-Situ Logic Execution Pipeline

When an agent passes dynamic logic bytecode (`.wasm` or JavaScript envelopes), the execution lifecycle enforces six distinct layers of defense:

1. **Layer 1 (Guardian AST)**: Parses and inspects the abstract syntax tree before execution. Only 14 standard functions from `wasi_snapshot_preview1` are permitted. Any attempt to reference unauthorized host symbols aborts immediately.
2. **Layer 2 (V8 Sandbox Isolation)**: Executes code inside an isolated V8 context where 25 potentially unsafe globals (`process`, `require`, `eval`, `Function`, `setTimeout`, `fetch`, `WebSocket`) are replaced with poisoned proxies that immediately trigger memory traps upon access. Eleven native prototypes (`Object`, `Array`, `Promise`, etc.) are frozen using `Object.freeze` to satisfy PCI-DSS limits.
3. **Layer 3 (Taint Analyzer)**: Acorn-based information flow control tracks variable assignments to prevent side-channel derivation of confidential inputs via boolean inference or character-code indexing.
4. **Layer 4 (Egress PII Shield)**: Scans outbound data against fuzzy matches, credit card patterns, IBAN formulas, and NER entity detection.
5. **Layer 5 (Aggregation-First Policy)**: Enforces that query outputs return summary statistics. Returning raw entity arrays triggers automatic policy rejection.
6. **Layer 6 (ZK-Receipt Generation)**: Computes an HMAC-SHA256 digest binding the returned output to the exact SHA-256 hash of the injected logic module, sealed using the ephemeral post-quantum session key.

---

## Exposing Data Resources & Prompts

In addition to executable capabilities, `LiopServer` exposes schemas, static references, and templated guidance to instruct AI agents.

### Publishing Resources

```typescript
server.resource(
  "Ledger Table Schema",
  "liop://schemas/financial/ledger.v1",
  "JSON schema describing fields and types in the internal ledger table.",
  "application/json",
  JSON.stringify({
    type: "object",
    properties: {
      tx_id: { type: "string" },
      timestamp: { type: "string", format: "date-time" },
      amount: { type: "number" },
      currency: { type: "string" },
    },
  }),
);
```

### Registering Prompts

```typescript
server.prompt(
  "audit_ledger_risk",
  "Instructs the agent on structuring in-situ WASM modules for ledger audits.",
  [
    { name: "accountId", description: "Target account identifier", required: true },
    { name: "strictness", description: "Audit tolerance level", required: false },
  ],
  (request) => ({
    description: "Ledger Risk Audit Template",
    messages: [
      {
        role: "user",
        content: {
          type: "text",
          text: `Evaluate account ${request.arguments?.accountId} with strictness ${request.arguments?.strictness ?? "standard"}. Output only aggregated statistics.`,
        },
      },
    ],
  }),
);
```

### Autonomous Prompt Injection (`enableZeroShotAutonomy`)

Activating autonomous mode injects the `liop_blind_analyst` system prompt and binds the host Data Dictionary dynamically:

```typescript
server.enableZeroShotAutonomy();
```

## Server Lifecycle & Network Binding

```typescript
// Start server on default or configured gRPC port
await server.connect();
console.log(`LiopServer listening on port ${server.getBoundPort()}`);

// Start server with explicit P2P Kademlia mesh bootstrap
await server.connectToMesh({
  port: 15021,
  meshConfig: {
    bootstrapNodes: ["/ip4/198.51.100.10/tcp/15001/p2p/12D3KooW..."],
    listenAddresses: ["/ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/15002"],
    identityPath: "/etc/liop/enclave-identity.json",
  },
});

// Invalidate in-memory AST cache when policies change
server.clearAstCache();

// Graceful termination
await server.close();
```

---

## Public Methods Reference

| Method | Parameters | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connect(port?)` | `port?: number` | `Promise<void>` | Binds gRPC server to port and begins accepting incoming intent handshakes. |
| `connectToMesh(options)` | `options: MeshConnectOptions` | `Promise<void>` | Boots both local gRPC service and full P2P `libp2p` DHT participant. |
| `tool(name, desc, schema, handler)` | `string, string, ZodRawShape, Handler` | `this` | Registers a typed capability with automatic input validation. |
| `resource(name, uri, desc, mime, content)` | `string, string, string, string, string` | `this` | Publishes a discoverable schema or static reference artifact. |
| `prompt(name, desc, args, handler)` | `string, string, PromptArg[], Handler` | `this` | Registers a structured prompt template for agent orchestration. |
| `enableZeroShotAutonomy()` | None | `this` | Injects the Blind Analyst prompt and internal data dictionary into the mesh. |
| `clearAstCache()` | None | `void` | Flushes parsed Guardian AST evaluation results from memory. |
| `getServerInfo()` | None | `{ name: string; version: string }` | Returns registered host identity metadata. |
| `getMeshNode()` | None | `MeshNode \| null` | Returns the active `libp2p` node instance when mesh mode is enabled. |
| `getBoundPort()` | None | `number` | Returns the assigned local TCP port of the running gRPC server. |
| `close()` | None | `Promise<void>` | Shuts down gRPC server, drains Piscina worker pool, and closes DHT sockets. |

# SECTION: TYPESCRIPT SDK GATEWAY (typescript-sdk/gateway.mdx)

---
title: "Gateway and Stream"
description: "Expose and route LIOP traffic with hybrid and stream bridges"
icon: "router"

---

The SDK includes transport components for routing MCP traffic across local and mesh environments.

## LiopHybridGateway

`LiopHybridGateway` multiplexes HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (gRPC) over a single TCP port and delegates MCP requests through `LiopMcpRouter`.

```typescript
import { LiopHybridGateway, LiopServer } from "@nekzus/liop";

const server = new LiopServer({ name: "gateway-node", version: "1.0.0" });
const gateway = new LiopHybridGateway(server, null, 50051);

await gateway.listen(3000);
// ... serve traffic
await gateway.stop();
```

## LiopMcpRouter & Dual-Era Compliance

`LiopMcpRouter` is the request dispatcher used by the gateway and CLI agents. It provides **Dual-Era MCP Protocol Compliance**:

- **Modern MCP v2 Era (2026-07-28)**: Supports stateless routing, non-polling resource updates via `subscriptions/listen`, dynamic resource template discovery (`resources/templates/list`), SEP-2243 header routing, and deterministically sorted results (SEP-2549).
- **Legacy MCP Era (2025-11-25)**: Automatically negotiates handshake capabilities and strips unsupported fields via `adaptResponseForLegacyClient()` for legacy MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor).
- **In-Situ Dispatch**: Routes calls to local tool definitions or discovers remote data providers across the Kademlia DHT mesh.
- **ZK Verification**: Automatically verifies HMAC-SHA256 ZK-Receipt commitments on incoming remote responses before returning results to the LLM.

## HTTP/1.1 gRPC-Web Framing Adapter

For edge networks, web browsers, and environments where native HTTP/2 gRPC framing is restricted by corporate firewalls or reverse proxies, `LiopHybridGateway` integrates an automatic **gRPC-Web framing adapter**:

- Emulates gRPC 5-byte length-prefixed binary frames (`[flags (1B)][length (4B BE)][payload]`) over standard HTTP/1.1 POST streams.
- Encodes gRPC status trailers in HTTP response headers (`grpc-status`, `grpc-message`).

## Observability & Health Probes

`LiopHybridGateway` natively serves standard Kubernetes and Prometheus endpoints:

| Endpoint | Protocol | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /healthz` | HTTP/1.1 | Liveness probe returning immediate JSON status (`{ status: "ok" }`) |
| `GET /readyz` | HTTP/1.1 | Readiness probe checking active DHT mesh connections and bootstrap sync |
| `GET /metrics` | HTTP/1.1 | Prometheus scraper endpoint reporting instantaneous connection gauges and latency histograms |
| `POST /mcp` | HTTP/1.1 (JSON-RPC) | Streamable MCP interface with session isolation and Zero-Trust bearer auth |

### Graceful Draining

When terminating nodes in production clusters:

```typescript
// Closes active listening sockets and allows in-flight RPCs to complete safely
await gateway.drain(5000); // 5-second graceful drain timeout
```

## LiopStreamBridge

`LiopStreamBridge` exposes a `LiopServer` over Streamable HTTP transport with session isolation.

```typescript
import { LiopServer, LiopStreamBridge } from "@nekzus/liop";

const server = new LiopServer({ name: "stream-node", version: "1.0.0" });
const stream = new LiopStreamBridge(server, {
  port: 3000,
  maxSessionsPerIp: 10,
  sessionTimeoutMs: 30 * 60 * 1000
});

await stream.start();
// ... streamable MCP traffic on /mcp
await stream.stop();
```

## Border LIO Gateway (BLG) & Perimeter Defense

In production topologies with multi-tier security domains, the **Border LIO Gateway (`blg`)** acts as the protocol boundary between external untrusted networks and Tier 1 sovereign enclaves:

```typescript
// Client invocation targeting Border LIO Gateway with OAuth 2.1 Bearer authentication
const tokenResponse = await fetch("http://nexus:3000/oidc/token", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
  body: new URLSearchParams({
    grant_type: "client_credentials",
    client_id: "border-gateway-client",
    client_secret: process.env.LIOP_BLG_SECRET || "default-secret"
  })
});

const { access_token, expires_in } = await tokenResponse.json();
// Bearer token is cached in memory with a 30s pre-expiration margin
```

### Gateway Responsibilities

1. **OAuth 2.1 Token Verification**: Asserts Bearer tokens signed by Nexus OIDC before proxying JSON-RPC requests to internal services.
2. **Swarm Key Bridge**: Possesses the private 256-bit PSK required to communicate directly with Tier 1 enclaves (`The Bank`, `The Vault`) across the isolated `pnet` subnet.
3. **Defense-in-Depth Inspection**: Runs preflight validation on AST logic payloads before dispatching to destination enclaves.

---

## Sliding-Window Rate Limiter (`InMemoryRateLimiter`)

To defend edge gateways, MCP endpoints, and worker pools against Denial of Service (DoS) attacks and brute-force token enumeration, the SDK provides a high-throughput, zero-dependency `InMemoryRateLimiter`.

It strictly adheres to **OWASP API Security Top 10 (API4:2023 - Unrestricted Resource Consumption)** by enforcing per-client sliding-window quotas.

```typescript
import { InMemoryRateLimiter } from "@nekzus/liop";

const limiter = new InMemoryRateLimiter({
  windowMs: 60_000,    // 1-minute evaluation window
  maxRequests: 120     // Up to 120 requests per window
});

// Middleware evaluation per incoming client IP or OAuth client ID
const status = limiter.check(req.socket.remoteAddress || "anonymous");
if (!status.allowed) {
  res.writeHead(429, {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Retry-After": Math.ceil(status.resetMs / 1000).toString(),
    "X-RateLimit-Limit": status.limit.toString(),
    "X-RateLimit-Remaining": status.remaining.toString(),
    "X-RateLimit-Reset": Math.ceil(status.resetMs / 1000).toString()
  });
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: "Too Many Requests", retryAfterMs: status.resetMs }));
  return;
}
```

### RateLimiter API Reference

| Method | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `check(key)` | `(key: string) => RateLimitStatus` | Evaluates whether the client quota allows another request. Returns remaining quota, status, and reset millisecond countdown. |
| `reset(key)` | `(key: string) => void` | Manually clears the bucket counter for a specific client key (useful post-successful MFA/OIDC challenge). |
| `cleanup()` | `() => void` | Prunes expired client records from the internal `Map` to prevent memory leaks during long-running sessions. |
| `close()` | `() => void` | Clears internal interval timers and destroys all cached quota buckets during graceful node shutdown. |

<Tip>
  The internal cleanup timer runs every 30 seconds and invokes `unref()`. This ensures the background maintenance loop never prevents the Node.js event loop from terminating cleanly during process exits or testing suites.
</Tip>

---

## Security Notes

- `LiopStreamBridge` supports Zero-Trust bearer enforcement via `ZERO_TRUST_TOKEN`.
- Sessions are isolated and evicted when idle to reduce long-lived attack surfaces.
- Gateway/router components preserve full MCP JSON-RPC compatibility while maintaining mesh-native routing behavior.
- The Border LIO Gateway caches RFC 6749 credentials in-memory with automatic refresh 30 seconds prior to expiration, eliminating transient 401 Unauthorized errors during high-frequency batch executions.
- For semantic perimeter filtering, see [Gateway Interceptor](/typescript-sdk/gateway-interceptor).


---

# SECTION: TYPESCRIPT SDK ECONOMY (typescript-sdk/economy.mdx)

---
title: "Economy and Telemetry"
description: "Measure token consumption and export observability metrics"
icon: "coins"

---

The SDK ships with a token economy module designed to estimate cost and expose telemetry for MCP operations.

## Estimators

The SDK includes a built-in, zero-runtime-dependency **`o200k_base`** Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer, the industry standard encoding scheme for modern OpenAI models (GPT-4o, o1, o3-mini) and an accurate baseline across major LLM providers (Anthropic Claude 3.5/3.7, Google Gemini 2.0).

Through build-time inlining and AST tree-shaking via `tsup`, the `o200k_base` vocabulary is bundled directly into the compiled distribution. This removes **25.95 MB** of external legacy tokenizer dependencies, reducing the installed `node_modules` footprint from **100.95 MB** to **84.43 MB** (-17.1% net reduction).

Both `createTokenEstimator()` (async factory) and `createSyncTokenEstimator()` (synchronous factory) provide immediate, synchronous access to `RealTokenEstimator` out-of-the-box:

```typescript
import {
  createTokenEstimator,
  createSyncTokenEstimator,
  RealTokenEstimator,
  HeuristicTokenEstimator
} from "@nekzus/liop";

// Instantly returns RealTokenEstimator ("o200k_base") synchronously
const syncEstimator = createSyncTokenEstimator();
console.log(syncEstimator.name); // "o200k_base"

// Exact BPE token counting with zero external runtime network or fs calls
const count = syncEstimator.countTokens("Hello world! Logic-Injection-on-Origin");
console.log(count); // 12

// Async factory for full API compatibility
const asyncEstimator = await createTokenEstimator();
```

<Note>
  `HeuristicTokenEstimator` (calculating `Math.ceil(chars / 4)`) remains available as a lightweight algorithmic fallback class if explicit heuristic modeling is desired.
</Note>

## TokenTelemetryEngine

`TokenTelemetryEngine` is a singleton collector for operation-level metrics:

- Input/output token estimates
- Operation type (`tools_list`, `tool_call`, `resource_read`, etc.)
- Duration metadata
- Session-level aggregates

```typescript
import { TokenTelemetryEngine } from "@nekzus/liop";

const telemetry = TokenTelemetryEngine.getInstance();
telemetry.record({
  type: "tool_call",
  method: "tools/call",
  estimatedInputTokens: 120,
  estimatedOutputTokens: 64
});
```

## LiopOTelBridge

`LiopOTelBridge` maps token telemetry into **OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.*` semantics** so external observability backends can ingest LIOP token data directly.

The bridge automatically binds to your global `MeterProvider` and emits the following metrics:
- `gen_ai.client.token.usage` (Histogram)
- `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` (Histogram)

Use this module when you need production cost visibility across local and mesh-routed MCP workloads.

## LiopMeshStatus Integration

The LIOP Agent exposes a local diagnostic tool called **`LiopMeshStatus`** that consumes the `TokenTelemetryEngine` internally to produce a structured operational status report via `formatStatusBlock()`. When an LLM calls this tool, it receives a structured report containing:

- **Session ID** and uptime
- **Estimator model** (`o200k_base` or heuristic)
- **Operation breakdown** (each MCP method called, with input/output token estimates)
- **Cumulative totals** (total tokens consumed across the session)
- **Cost projection** (estimated cost based on configurable per-token pricing)

<Tip>
  The token economy telemetry is **intentionally visible** in the `LiopMeshStatus` output. This transparency enables B2B clients to audit consumption patterns and allows AI agents to autonomously manage their context window budgets without requiring external monitoring infrastructure.
</Tip>

---

## Deterministic AST Fuel Metering

In addition to token estimation, the SDK provides deterministic computational fuel measurement via `calculateAstInstructionFuel`:

```typescript
import { calculateAstInstructionFuel } from "@nekzus/liop";

const javascriptCode = `
  const total = env.records.reduce((acc, r) => acc + r.amount, 0);
  return { count: env.records.length, average: total / env.records.length };
`;

// Parses Acorn AST, evaluates instruction weight, and quantizes to 100-unit buckets
const fuel = calculateAstInstructionFuel(javascriptCode);
console.log(fuel); // 500 units
```

### Side-Channel Timing Invariance (NIST SP 800-53)

To ensure zero timing leakage across varying private inputs, `calculateAstInstructionFuel` enforces 100-unit bucket quantization:

$$\text{Fuel} = \lceil \frac{\text{RawASTScore}}{100} \rceil \times 100$$

Across extensive automated profiling (50 consecutive executions on synthetic transaction batches), payloads with identical AST topology evaluating divergent secret inputs yield a standard deviation of strictly zero (`stddev = 0`).

---

## Context & Token Economy vs Traditional MCP (Context-Pulling)

Traditional MCP requires pulling entire raw datasets across the network into the LLM context window before filtering or analysis can occur. LIOP executes sandboxed logic directly on the origin node, returning only aggregated proofs.

### Empirical Efficiency Comparison

| Metric | Traditional MCP (Context-Pulling) | LIOP (Logic-on-Origin) | Net Savings |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Paradigm** | Raw Data Extraction to Agent | Sandboxed WASI Execution in Origin | **Zero Data Egress** |
| **Input Context Tokens** | ~16,000 – 48,000 tokens | ~320 – 650 tokens | **98.9% – 99.3% reduction** |
| **Output Context Tokens** | ~1,200 – 4,500 tokens | ~80 – 180 tokens | **93.3% – 96.0% reduction** |
| **Network Wire Transfer** | ~195 KB (raw JSON payload) | ~801 B (gRPC envelope + receipt) | **99.6% reduction** |
| **LLM Context Saturation** | High (triggers truncation / sliding window) | Minimal (preserves reasoning capacity) | **Zero Context Bloat** |
| **PII / Exfiltration Risk** | Severe (raw records leave perimeter) | Zero (blocked by 6-layer shield) | **Cryptographically Sealed** |

---

curl -X GET http://localhost:16000/api/telemetry
```

    },

    }
  }
}
```
